title: www.anas.studio must redirect to the apex before the store opens: every function accepts only SITE_URL's origin
why_needed: P11 says to take anas.studio and www off the soon Worker and attach them to the Pages project (PLANS/WORK-PACKAGES.md:143, SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md:49) and nothing plans a www → apex redirect. The checkout, payments (verify), orders, download, notify and contact functions answer CORS for one origin and refuse any other with 403 (`siteOrigin()` in supabase/functions/_shared/http.ts:38; checkout.ts:250, payments.ts verify, orders.ts:147, notify.ts:105), and Turnstile checks the apex hostname. If www serves the site, a buyer on www.anas.studio gets «تعذّر تحديث الأسعار» in the cart, cannot check out, and the return, order and notification pages fail. Cloudflare documents the www → apex redirect for Pages as a Bulk Redirect plus a proxied www record, not a second custom domain (developers.cloudflare.com/pages/how-to/www-redirect/).
touches: P11 launch steps and docs/deployment.md (Bulk Redirect www → https://anas.studio preserving path and query; www DNS record proxied); a hosted check that https://www.anas.studio/store answers 301 to the apex

title: IP throttles of the buyer path against Saudi mobile carrier NAT at launch
why_needed: The buyer path is throttled per public IP: create 10 per hour (checkout_create, 20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:479), quote 300 per hour (checkout_payment.sql:346), verify 120 per hour (payment_core.sql:1282), order page 120 per hour (delivery.sql:85). Saudi mobile carriers put many subscribers behind shared IPv4 addresses (carrier-grade NAT), so at a book launch the 11th buyer of the hour on one carrier address is refused with «أرسلت طلبات كثيرة؛ حاول لاحقًا.» and cannot buy for up to an hour. DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:69 asks that IP throttling stay secondary so shared networks remain usable and that concrete thresholds be recorded; no plan item checks these numbers against shared-address traffic before the switch opens.
touches: the four SQL thresholds (or an IPv4 allowance much higher than IPv6 /64's), docs/payments-runbook.md, a load note in P10/P11
